context.section_tech_spec_epic_2_relevance: This story directly addresses Acceptance Criteria 6 and 7 from `tech-spec-epic-2.md`: - "The user can delete a course, which soft-deletes it in the database." - "Soft-deleted courses do not appear in the main course list." The implementation should leverage the `softDeleteCourse` method defined in the `ICourseManager` interface. The `courses` table includes a `deleted_at TIMESTAMPTZ` column for this purpose, and queries for active courses must filter `deleted_at IS NULL`.
context.section_architecture_relevance: As per `solution-architecture.md`, the Next.js frontend will communicate directly with Supabase via `supabase-js`. All database operations for courses are protected by Row Level Security (RLS) policies to ensure users can only modify their own courses. The `softDeleteCourse` operation will be an `UPDATE` query that sets the `deleted_at` timestamp.

code_snippets.sql_table_definition: CREATE TABLE public.courses ( id BIGINT PRIMARY KEY GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY, user_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES public.users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, name TEXT NOT NULL, syllabus TEXT, exam_date DATE, deleted_at TIMESTAMPTZ, -- Crucial for soft delete created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT NOW() );

sql_rls_policy.name: Enable all access for own courses

code_snippets.sql_rls_policy: CREATE POLICY "Enable all access for own courses" ON public.courses FOR ALL USING (auth.uid() = user_id);
code_snippets.javascript_supabase_filter_example: // Example of fetching active courses const { data: courses, error } = await supabase .from('courses') .select('*') .is('deleted_at', null); // Filter for non-deleted courses

context.ui_ux_considerations: The UI for deleting a course should: - Provide an easily discoverable "Delete" action (e.g., an icon or button) next to each course. - Implement a high-friction confirmation modal or dialog to prevent accidental data loss. This modal must require the user to explicitly type the course's name to enable the final "Soft-Delete" button. The dialog should also clearly communicate the consequences (course will disappear from the active list) and the possibility of restoration (mentioning the 30-day window). - Provide clear visual feedback upon successful deletion (e.g., the course immediately disappears from the list, a temporary toast notification).
context.developer_notes: - Ensure the `softDeleteCourse` method performs an `UPDATE` operation on the `public.courses` table, setting the `deleted_at` column to `NOW()` or `new Date().toISOString()`. - Implement the high-friction confirmation modal as described in the UI/UX considerations, including the requirement for the user to type the course name. - Verify that all queries used to display the active course list consistently include the `is('deleted_at', null)` filter. - Thoroughly test RLS: ensure a user cannot soft-delete a course belonging to another user. - Consider error handling and displaying user-friendly messages for failed delete operations.
